correctness.rationale: The uniform-primitive-rotation identity is exact. The selected minimal length-ell window survives all fixed predecessor-bit edits outside an O_h(log n/sqrt n) bad event: an edited competing length-ell window would require a second disjoint approximate k-zero run, whose union-bound probability is n(ell+h)2^(-2k+h-1). The good event is invariant under all edits, proving exact equiprobability within it; fixed prefix freezing follows from existence of a length-k zero-run. Cyclic block count preservation and disjoint-trial concentration yield interior neighborhood saturation. Effective bounded-degree Hanf locality then proves an effective dyadic limit for every fixed FO sentence. Every dyadic value is realized by explicit terminal predicates. The supplementary checker verified 131068 finite words with 8798 Lyndon representatives. No simulation is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The claim is about complete successor-first-order limiting probabilities of a uniform nonregular Lyndon family, based on a quantitative robust predecessor-window switching lemma. The inspected same-object papers study factor lengths, while recent logical-limit work concerns small permutation classes and regular-language encodings. The result is not claimed novel merely because its numerical spectrum is dyadic; the structural reduction and exact model-specific classification are essential. Historical priority remains a stated risk.

value.rationale: Canonical Lyndon representatives are nonregular and selected by a global extremal rotation. The theorem quantitatively proves that successor-first-order truth ignores this global selection except for an explicitly characterized terminal random boundary. It determines every asymptotic sentence probability effectively and gives the exact full spectrum, not an arbitrary finite slice or a re-expression of pre-existing total-count enumerations.
